lm.prediction.W1-01: At a paid-leave headcount threshold, excess mass immediately below the cutoff is greater where affiliate aggregation is not stated than where it is explicit.
lm.prediction.W1-02: New legal entities per continuing parent increase near an unaggregated threshold more than near an explicitly aggregated threshold.
lm.prediction.W1-03: A verified amendment closing an affiliate-splitting route reduces threshold bunching relative to unchanged thresholds.
lm.prediction.W1-04: Where contractors are excluded, transitions from employee to legally excluded contractor status rise around commencement relative to comparable covered classes.
lm.prediction.W1-05: Explicit seasonal or per-diem exclusions predict increased use of genuinely excluded classes relative to covered classes at commencement.
lm.prediction.W1-06: Use waiting periods predict more separations in the final {days} days before entitlement than in the following {days} days, relative to laws without a use waiting period.
lm.prediction.W1-07: Paid-leave cap tiers predict greater excess mass below a size threshold than a law with no size-dependent cap tier.
lm.prediction.W1-08: A reference-week counting rule predicts more employment dips in the statutory reference week than in adjacent weeks, relative to annual-average counting rules.
lm.prediction.W1-09: Prospective-only noncompete reforms predict a contract-signing surge before the verified applicability cutoff relative to reforms governing existing contracts.
lm.prediction.W1-10: A verified grandfathered collective agreement cutoff predicts earlier renewals among affected agreements relative to agreements not grandfathered.
lm.prediction.W1-11: Text-predicted avoidance routes improve held-out classification of the frozen behavioral events over employer size and industry alone.
lm.prediction.W1-12: Explicit anti-headcount-reduction clauses predict smaller reference-period headcount dips than otherwise comparable laws lacking an explicit clause.
